name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,315

entries.clue: Means of winding up former partner with court summons (10)

indicatorNotes.with: puts the second piece alongside the first

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a citation is a summons to appear in court

annotation.surface: A bitter divorcee serves papers on an ex just to get under their skin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Winding up' reads as the end of a marriage or a company, but here it is teasing someone until they get worked up.
annotation.definitionFit: Excitation is the act of stirring someone up, which is exactly what winding them up does.

entries.clue: Anticipate tirades about old medicines (12)

indicatorNotes.about: the tirades sit about, next to, the old: O goes up against RANTS

annotation.surface: Someone braces for an earful of complaints about outdated pills.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About old medicines' looks like the topic of the tirades; the definition is only the last word, and O simply joins RANTS.
annotation.definitionFit: Expectorants are cough medicines that help you bring up phlegm.

entries.clue: Chap last to consider protection provided by insurance (5)

indicatorNotes.last to: takes only the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: cove is old British slang for a chap, a fellow

annotation.surface: A man is the final one to weigh up what his insurance policy covers.
annotation.walkthrough: Cove is dated British slang for a man, a regular stand-in for 'chap' in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the insurance industry's own word for what a policy protects you against.

entries.clue: Rubbish bit of indelible body art (3)

indicatorNotes.bit of: only a part of the word is taken, its first three letters

blocks.note: British slang for cheap, tacky goods
TATTOO cut down to its first part

annotation.surface: Someone sneers at a poorly done tattoo as rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: Indelible body art is a tattoo; 'bit of' keeps just its opening TAT. Tat is British for tacky, worthless stuff.
annotation.definitionFit: Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods, that is, rubbish.

entries.clue: Tasteless attempt to conceal evidence of fire (6)

indicatorNotes.to conceal: the attempt hides the next piece inside it

blocks.note: ash is what a fire leaves behind

annotation.surface: An arsonist makes a crude effort to cover up the traces.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a cover-up after a fire, and 'tasteless' is not about food here but about style.
annotation.definitionFit: Trashy means cheap and in poor taste.

entries.clue: Bad few months early in the year for kids (9)

blocks.note: food that has gone bad has gone off

blocks.clueFragment: few months early in the year
blocks.note: spring is the season early in the year

annotation.surface: The start of the year is a rough stretch for children.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kids' could be young goats, but here they are children; 'off' is bad in the sense of spoiled milk.
annotation.definitionFit: Offspring are one's children, one's kids.

entries.clue: Stayed in the sack, devouring papers? (6)

indicatorNotes.devouring: one piece swallows the other, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: in the sack = in bed = abed

annotation.surface: Someone lies in bed all morning reading the newspapers.
annotation.walkthrough: The papers are not newspapers but identity documents, ID; 'the sack' is slang for bed.
annotation.definitionFit: To abide is to stay or remain, so abided = stayed.

entries.clue: Exhibited one’s feelings, as strange dreams tend to (12)

indicatorNotes.strange: the letters that follow are put into a strange, unfamiliar order

annotation.surface: A dreamer's emotions ran wild, just as odd dreams tend to make them do.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder runs through 'to' at the very end; stopping at 'tend' leaves you two letters short.
annotation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is to show feelings openly, as in a demonstrative person.

entries.clue: Turn to significant person (when taken aback) (5)

indicatorNotes.when taken aback: aback = backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a VIP is a very important person

annotation.surface: Someone swings round to face an important figure, startled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' in the surface means surprised, but it tells you to read TO VIP backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, verb for verb: to rotate about a fixed point.

entries.clue: Pleasant story following football organisation making a comeback (7)

indicatorNotes.following: the story comes after the next piece
indicatorNotes.making a comeback: comes back the other way, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: the FA, the Football Association, runs English football

annotation.surface: A cheering tale about a football body's return to form.
annotation.walkthrough: The FA is the Football Association, the body that governs football in England. 'Comeback' sounds like a sporting revival, but it turns FA into AF.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a person who is good-natured and easy to talk to.

entries.clue: Big container vessel in new cigar shop (5,4)

indicatorNotes.new: the letters are made into something new, rearranged

annotation.surface: A huge humidor jar on display in a newly opened tobacconist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Container vessel' could be a jar in the shop, but it is a ship that carries shipping containers.
annotation.definitionFit: A cargo ship is a large vessel carrying containers of goods.

entries.clue: Exaggerate more than some types initially had (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of the words it governs

blocks.note: the first letters of Some Types
had, as in had dinner = ate

annotation.surface: Someone boasts of having more than a few typefaces to begin with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had' is the easy one to miss: had a meal, so ATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to claim more than the facts support.

entries.clue: Two people jointly told you so at the end (3)

indicatorNotes.at the end: take the end letter of each word

blocks.clueFragment: told you so at the end
blocks.note: the last letters of tolD yoU sO

annotation.surface: A pair say 'I told you so' together once it is all over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Told you so' is so familiar a phrase that it reads as speech, not as three words to take the tails of.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used especially of performers who work as a pair.

entries.clue: Nothing good is held in reserve (2,3)

annotation.surface: A gloomy proverb: nothing good is ever kept back.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a complete sentence; split it after 'good' and 'is' becomes a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Something put on ice is set aside and kept in reserve for later.

entries.clue: Revenue of millions netted by fashionable company (European) (6)

indicatorNotes.netted by: caught in a net, so the letter goes inside the rest

annotation.surface: A trendy European firm reports millions in revenue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Netted' looks like the accounting sense, net profit, in a clue about revenue, but it means caught in a net.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the money a person or business takes in.

entries.clue: Body of water in south of France, running to the west (5)

indicatorNotes.running to the west: in an across clue, west is leftwards, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A description of a lake or bay in the south of France, with a westward current.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South of France' is not the Riviera but the French word for south, SUD. The Indus is a great river of Pakistan.
annotation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river, a body of water, flowing through Pakistan.

entries.clue: List of charges to row across a river (6)

indicatorNotes.across: the row stretches across, around, the next pieces

blocks.note: a tiff is a row, a quarrel

annotation.surface: A boatman's price list for rowing people over a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a quarrel (rhymes with cow), not what you do with oars.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the word hotels and utilities use for their published price schedule.

entries.clue: Endlessly mischievous way in which a situation develops (3)

annotation.definition: way in which a situation develops

indicatorNotes.Endlessly: without its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: ARCH (mischievous, as in an arch look) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A situation keeps developing in an ever more mischievous direction.
annotation.walkthrough: Arch means playfully mischievous, as in an arch smile.
annotation.definitionFit: An arc is the shape of a story's development, as in a narrative arc.

entries.clue: Carnage is ultimately music to a comedian’s ear? (9)

blocks.note: what a comedian loves to hear

annotation.surface: A dark joke: bloodshed as the thing a comic most wants to hear.
annotation.walkthrough: Comedians talk of killing an audience or slaying them, so carnage is a comedian's word for success.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean killing on a large scale.

entries.clue: Portion of rent he takes for letter (5)

indicatorNotes.Portion of: only part of the phrase is taken, the letters inside it

annotation.surface: A landlord pockets part of the rent in exchange for a letter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like mail in a landlord story, but it is a Greek letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Main pit reconfigured for percussion instruments (7)

annotation.surface: An orchestra pit is rearranged to fit in the drums.
annotation.walkthrough: The pit is the orchestra pit, so the fodder belongs to the answer's own world.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: kettledrums, tuned drums at the back of an orchestra.

entries.clue: Top clubs are supported (5)

blocks.note: things that rest on something are supported by it

annotation.surface: The best clubs have backing behind them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' looks like sports teams, but it is the card suit, C.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as nouns: the highest point of a hill or wave.

entries.clue: Stick that could break? (3)

blocks.note: not a twig or a walking stick but the long tapered rod used on a snooker or pool table
not snap: in snooker and pool a break is the opening shot, or a run of scoring shots

annotation.surface: A flimsy stick that might snap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Break' suggests snapping, but in snooker and pool a break is a run of scoring shots, or the opening shot, made with a CUE.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the snooker player's stick is the thing that makes a break, not the thing that suffers one.

entries.clue: Various red flags, including extremes of resistance and narcissism (4,6)

indicatorNotes.Various: the letters are arranged in various ways, mixed
indicatorNotes.including: adds the next letters into the mix
indicatorNotes.extremes of: the outer letters of the word

annotation.surface: A list of warning signs in a partner, among them stubbornness and vanity.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is dating advice, with narcissism looking like one more red flag; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Self-regard is excessive admiration of oneself, narcissism.
